messages:
Incident Bot: [ALERT] High 429s from GPU hotpool - sustained for 7m · affected.region=us-west-2 · approx 18% of requests getting 429. Pager duty triggered. Runbook: https://playbooks/internal/hotpool-surge
Priya Rao (oncall): Ack. I’m on it, joining call in 2m. @Mira @Evan can you grab metrics while I pull runbook?
Mira Patel: Looking at dashboards — queue length for hotpath has grown from ~40 -> ~420 in last 6m. Avg p99 latency spiked to 1.8s then cascaded to 12s before 429 ramp. GPU pool hotpool-west-2a shows 0 free slots.
Evan Liu: Autoscaler logs show repeated "scale-request-denied: tier-limit" entries. Looks like tier policy rejected additional nodes because burst_quota for tier "standard" is set to 0.5 units/min and we hit that.
Jonah Kim: Also seeing autoscaler worker failing to claim new instances: 
```
2026-03-15T12:10:05Z autoscaler-v2 ERROR claim failed: quota exceeded for project:redwood-core
2026-03-15T12:10:06Z autoscaler-v2 WARN tier-policy mismatch: requested=hotpath, allowed=standard
```
Priya Rao (oncall): @Jonah are we hitting cloud quota or internal tier gating? Which is the blocker?
Jonah Kim: Both. Cloud quota for GPU cores in us-west-2 is near limit for the org (we're at 94%). BUT autoscaler is also refusing to move requests to dedicated/backfill pools because the tier policy mapping is too strict — hotpath requests are pinned to "hotpath" tier but that tier has a very low token refill config.
Mira Patel: Confirmed token refill rate for hotpath tier: `refill=2 tokens/min, burst=4` — with current qps that under-provisions. Old configs from last patch changed rates accidentally.
Priya Rao (oncall): Ok immediate mitigation options: 1) loosen tier policy to allow hotpath -> reserved fallback (if reserved has capacity), 2) increase token refill for hotpath temporarily, 3) enable model-fallback routing to smaller model to reduce GPU time per request. Which is fastest?
Evan Liu: Easiest: bump refill to 20/min and burst to 50 for hotpath. That requires a config push but no infra changes. Could do in <5m.
Nate (eng-runtime): We can also flip routing to allow hotpath->dedicated-backfill. Need a config change in routing policies: `allow_fallback:true` for route /v1/generate:hotpath. Can roll in <3m. If cloud quota prevents new GPUs, fallback will still relieve pressure by sending some load to dedicated instances that do have capacity.
Priya Rao (oncall): Do it. Mira do the token bump, Nate do routing fallback, Jonah keep watching autoscaler->cloud quota. I’ll start customer impact note.
Mira Patel: Pushing change now — config snippet pushed: 
```
routes:
  hotpath:
    tier: hotpath
    tokens:
      refill_per_min: 20
      burst: 50
```
Mira Patel: Change applied and hot reload triggered. Observability: queue length started to drop — 420 -> 260 in 90s. 429 rate falling from 18% -> 6%.
Nate (eng-runtime): Routing fallback enabled: `allow_fallback:true` for hotpath. A/B routing sending ~15% of hotpath to dedicated-backfill. Latency on fallback path is 2x but fewer 429s.
Jonah Kim: Cloud quota still at 94% — we can’t rely on adding GPUs. Filed quota escalation ticket with infra cloud team: https://tickets/internal/INC-2419 (pinging infra).
Priya Rao (oncall): Good. Quick customer impact summary for status page: "We experienced elevated 429 errors for GPU-backed requests in us-west-2 due to a combination of strict tier token settings and cloud quota saturation. Mitigations applied: temporary token refill bump and routing fallback to reserved capacity. Errors decreasing and queue draining. No data loss." Anyone want to tweak wording before I post?
Support Ops Bot: /post-update channel=#status: "Investigating elevated 429s affecting GPU requests in US-WEST-2. Mitigations in progress."
Evan Liu: One follow-up: we should not keep the high refill config long-term — it erodes fairness across tenants. Plan to revert to safe defaults after traffic normalizes and after quota relief. Add a canary window and rate-limit slack to 10% of burst for non-critical tenants.
Mira Patel: Agree. Also we need a post-incident action: audit recent config PR that changed hotpath tokens (PR #4621 changed units from tokens/sec -> tokens/min accidentally).
Jonah Kim: Autoscaler improvement: fall back to preemptible GPU pool when standard quota reached and degrade p99 gracefully. Put item on eng-runtime backlog.
Priya Rao (oncall): Oncall handoff: I’ll stay on this for another 20m, then hand over to Jonah for overnight monitoring. @Jonah you okay?
Jonah Kim: Yep, I’ll take overnight. Will keep alerts with tighter thresholds.
Nate (eng-runtime): I’ll draft runbook changes: add step to validate tier token units and a quick toggle to enable allow_fallback for routing.
Priya Rao (oncall): Thanks everyone. Final numbers at 12:47Z: 429s from 18% -> 1.2%, queue length 420 -> 28, p99 latency back down to ~950ms. I’ll post customer-facing update and start a follow-up incident review tomorrow.
Incident Bot: Incident resolved by mitigation actions — severity reduced to SEV3. Runbook link: https://playbooks/internal/hotpool-surge — please attach postmortem notes.
Priya Rao (oncall): Posting summary to #incidents-postmortems and scheduling a 1h RCA tomorrow 09:00 PT. Closing thread here. :white_check_mark:
